observations: Order is the all-box puzzle: two forks, each with a dead end to do first (fork-1 Nitro room, fork-2 crystal block before the one-way drop).
Body-slam walls are count banks: 22 of 62 main boxes in two hazard-free walls; the risk is in the routing (dead end, one-way hole).
Explosives frame single rewards (the ? between Nitros; the ? stack beside a Nitro stack), never guard big groups.
Both Aku boxes come early; the second sits at fork 1, right before the Nitro room.
Secret content does not tax the all-box goal: the secret course holds only 3 Nitros cleared remotely by the green !.
The Nitro switch sits at the start of the finale beside C3, so the count is settled before the last segment.
Teaching beats sit at checkpoints and in the bonus (striped sandwich at C1; ! switch, steel-hemmed slam, arrow-to-ceiling bounce in the bonus).
Main density 11/16/31/4: a spike from the two walls, then a navigation-only finale.
Every box group sits in a calm room between hazard tunnels: hazard corridor, then payout room.
openQuestions: Fork-1 Nitro room count (12) is a residual of the two wall estimates.
Bonus B-x (3 boxes) unlocated; outline boxes' count status unknown.
S3-e may contain one striped box.

geometryObservations: two room types alternate: pipes are slide tests (fans, rolling enemies), pool rooms are timing tests (eel discharges); crates sit in the calm walkways between
the pool is one gap re-dressed five times: wide waiting walkways, sinking pads, a mid-pool waiting platform, no footing with floating Nitro, five floating platforms (secret)
the eel is the pool's clock and the water is the telegraph (yellow flashing); the counter is to enter as the flash ends and leave fast
fans are gates with an enemy key: sliding a scrubber or knocking a rat into a fan breaks a blade
counters are taught in contradiction (scrubber: spin/slide; spiky rat: no spin), then mixed one after another (POINT 9)
rolling barrels use the pipe's curvature as a pendulum; the reprise puts a rat in the waiting spot between two barrels (POINT 10)
Nitro is architecture: edge stacks narrow walkways, the Nitro room builds a 1-u lane and a 2-high hurdle and hides a secret door, floating Nitro replace stepping stones
each fork pairs a dead end with a through route; fork 2's through route ends in a one-way hole, so geometry enforces dead end first
the point of no return (floor hole) lies between the player and the last payout wall
the finale swaps movement mode: hand-over-hand is safe from falls but slow, so indestructible mines become wait-then-outpace gates
mines escalate by behaviour: patrolling, sentry, hovering beside a landing, three static (announced easy beat), two bobbing under a low ceiling
the low ceiling punishes the over-jump: the last gate is passed with a regular jump; a dash-jump is fatal (D2)
geometryTransfer: timed pool as a phasepad crossing over a 5-6 m pit (3-4 s cycle, 0.9 s warning): wide waiting ledge first, then a one-two pad pair, then a mid-crossing safe pad, then a crossing between floating Nitro
rocking-barrel tube: a pendulum swinging across a 5-6 m tube (pass while the bob is high on one side); reprise with a grunt in the waiting spot between two pendulums (stone rolls only along Z)
counter-switch corridor: alternate grunt (spin) and spiker (stomp only) every 4-6 m in a 4 m corridor after teaching each alone
on-foot Nitro room: a ? between two Nitro (one 1.152 m lane) and a 2-high Nitro hurdle (2.3 m: full jump on foot clears it, a board ollie cannot); mask crate before it
one-way drop in front of the last payout: a 2-3 m floor hole between the player and a 2 x 6 crate wall, the drop leading to the next checkpoint
height-capped final gate: a ceiling at 4.2-4.6 m (above full-jump head reach 3.8 m, below double-jump 5.5 m) over a hazard crossed by one full jump
